messages:
elena: Thanks for joining the live follow-up from todays all-hands. Opening this thread for brief Q&A on leadership direction, positioning, market focus, and competitor questions. Ill answer quickly here and follow up with a short doc. :wave:

matt_p: Two quick questions: 1) mission  still "developer-first"? 2) are we changing our product-led approach if enterprise asks ramp up?

elena: Mission stays developer-first. PLG remains our primary motion; were layering enterprise-friendly controls (SLA contracts, private deploy) not replacing PLG. Think: self-serve for adoption, sales-assisted for scale.

sophia_r: How should we summarize our tangible advantage vs big cloud endpoints in one sentence for customers?

elena: "Same API everywhere, cost controls you can see and tune, and built-for-production reliability." Keep it simple.

raj: Competitor angle: how do we position against fast-moving open-source runtimes that promise cheap inference?

elena: Acknowledge cost claims but emphasize operational burden: we sell predictable economics + observability + fallbacks. Most teams value time-to-production + reliability.

calvin: Can we get a short competitor cheat sheet (two lines each) for sales? They ask on calls a lot.

elena: Yes  Ill coordinate with Matt to produce a 1-slide cheat sheet: bullets on cloud managed endpoints, OSS runtimes, and API-first LLM providers.

priya: Roadmap focus: should we accelerate multimodal support or finish autoscaling and better caching? Customers want both but teams are small.

elena: Near-term priority: autoscaling improvements, cache diagnostics, and buildouts that reduce unit cost for current text workloads. Multimodal is on the roadmap but gated by reliability and performance parity.

matt_p: Pricing question: any changes coming for hosted per-token billing or discounts for committed usage?

elena: Hosted stays per-token; were adding committed-capacity and committed-discount plans for Dedicated, plus contract-level discounts for enterprise.

sophia_r: For messaging: how strongly do we call out "unified runtime" in public docs vs internal decks?

elena: Public: highlight consistency across deployments and how it reduces migration risk. Internal: emphasize routing, rollout, and caching tech details.

raj: Quick product governance Q: what bar must a new open model clear to be added to our catalog?
elena: Performance on our infra, license compatibility, and quality tests on representative prompts. Community adoption is a tie-breaker.

calvin: Any change to partner strategy? More marketplaces or direct SI partnerships?

elena: Targeted marketplace listings + strategic SI/ISV partners for regulated verticals. Not every partner  only the ones that reduce friction for customers.

priya: Could leadership publish the 4 biggest talking points for sales and a 1-page FAQ?

elena: Yes. Ill drop a 1-page FAQ and 4 bullets for sales into the enablement folder by EOD tomorrow and ping this thread.

jen_bot: Note: all-hands recording uploaded (https://drive.internal/redwood/all-hands/177999).

elena: Thanks all  short and useful. If you need deeper follow-up, DM me or schedule 15. Ill post the cheat sheet and FAQ shortly. :rocket:
